# Adjudication Task — Chapter 871

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃871화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|동창과 함께 황제의 수족이라 불리는 금의위라 해도 정해진 한계는 있었던 모양이다.
  6|
  7|정호군은 이름 모를 쌍둥이 중년인에게 나와 상산왕을 인도하며 짧은 전음을 남겼다.
  8|
  9|- 지금부터는 말 한마디, 행동 하나하나에 신중해야 할 것이다. 그렇지 않다면 결코 살아서 나올 수 없을 테니.
 10|
 11|시벌놈이 누굴 놀리나.
 12|
 13|그렇지 않아도 이미 피부로 생생하게 느끼는 중이다.
 14|
 15|난데없이 나타난 저 쌍둥이 초절정 고수는 물론이고, 아직 들어서지도 않은 궁 내부의 수많은 인기척까지.
 16|
 17|‘더럽게 삼엄하네.’
 18|
 19|모래라도 삼킨 것처럼 입안이 텁텁하다. 나는 눈치채지 못할 만큼 천천히 공력을 끌어올리며 입술을 달싹였다.
 20|
 21|- 하나만 묻자. 도대체 날 부른 이유가 뭐지?
 22|
 23|- 모른다고 했을 텐데.
 24|
 25|- 정말 몰라서 모른다고 하는 거야, 아니면 알아도 모르는 거야?
 26|
 27|- 둘 다.
 28|
 29|빌어먹을. 물어본 내가 등신이지.
 30|
 31|나는 언제나처럼 무뚝뚝한 얼굴로 서 있는 정호군을 노려본 뒤, 사인교에서 내린 상산왕과 함께 건청궁(乾淸宮)이라고 적힌 현판을 지나쳤다.
 32|
 33|저벅. 저벅.
 34|
 35|유난히도 크게 울려 퍼지는 발걸음 소리.
 36|
 37|나는 한 치의 오차도 없이 똑같은 움직임으로 나아가는 쌍둥이의 뒷모습을 보며 조용히 가늠했다.
 38|
 39|‘합격술(合擊術)을 익힌 게 틀림없는데…… 정확히 무슨 무공을 익힌 거지?’
 40|
 41|아무리 생각해도 상황이 좋지 않다.
 42|
 43|상대가 익힌 무공을 유추할 수 없다는 것은 둘째치고, 이미 완숙한 경지에 오른 두 명의 초절정 고수가 펼치는 합격술은 상상만 해도 속이 쓰렸다.
 44|
 45|게다가…….
 46|
 47|‘뭔 놈의 박쥐 새끼들이 이렇게 많은지.’
 48|
 49|은은한 불빛 속에서도 드러나지 않은 그림자들.
 50|
 51|어둠 속에서 모든 일거수일투족을 감시하고 있는 저들은 황실에서 키워 낸 호위이자 살수(殺手)가 틀림없다.
 52|
 53|그리고 만약 최악의 상황이 닥친다면, 무려 일백에 달하는 저 살수들은 평생을 연마해 온 일격필살의 수법으로 나를 난자할 것이다.
 54|
 55|뱃속에서부터 합격술을 익혔을 것 같은 쌍둥이 초절정 고수와 함께.
 56|
 57|‘십왕(十王). 아니, 어쩌면 삼성(三星)에 버금가는 고수가 아닌 이상 십중팔구는 이곳에서 뼈를 묻는다.’
 58|
 59|세인들은 말한다. 무림은 도산검림(刀山劍林)의 세상이라고.
 60|
 61|하지만 틀렸다.
 62|
 63|이곳이야말로 진정한 도산검림이다. 오직 황제의 뜻에 따라 생사가 결정되는 공간.
 64|
 65|‘도대체 얼마나 많은 고수를 거느린 거지?’
 66|
 67|명문대파로 불리는 구파일방과 오대세가가 많아야 둘. 기껏해야 한 명 정도를 보유하고 있는 초절정 고수를 무려 둘이나 문지기로 부리다니.
 68|
 69|마치 칼날 위를 걷는 듯한 기분이다.
 70|
 71|나도 모르는 사이에 식은땀 한 방울이 목덜미를 타고 흘러내린 그때. 나는 문득 어느 자그마한 손에 의해 옷소매가 당겨지고 있음을 깨달았다.
 72|
 73|꾸욱.
 74|
 75|옷소매가 구겨지도록 힘주어 움켜잡은 손. 그제야 어린 왕의 가파른 호흡이 느껴진다.
 76|
 77|‘떨고 있어.’
 78|
 79|황족이고, 왕이기 전에 어린아이다.
 80|
 81|처음 만났던 그때에도 그랬고, 지금도 다르지 않았다.
 82|
 83|기억도 나지 않을 만큼 어린 시절에 황궁을 떠났다고 했으니, 당연히 천자에 대한 기억도 없겠지.
 84|
 85|‘그런데 이제는 유일한 가족이자, 하나뿐인 형에게 목숨을 위협받는 중이고.’
 86|
 87|문득 그런 생각이 들었다.
 88|
 89|황도까지 오는 길에 상산왕이 보였던 낙천적인 모습은, 어쩌면 그런 두려움과 실망을 감추기 위한 노력이 아니었을까 하는 생각이.
 90|
 91|천자의 위협을 경고하는 홍진의 말에도 그럴 리 없다며 고개를 내젓던 그 모습은, 믿기 힘든 현실을 마주한 어린아이가 할 수 있는 유일한 선택이었을지도 모르겠다.
 92|
 93|‘분명 아무것도 몰라야 할 아이인데…… 철이 너무 일찍 들어 버렸어.’
 94|
 95|마음이 복잡해졌다.
 96|
 97|칼바람이 휘몰아치던 산서성의 그해 겨울, 부모를 잃고 고사리 같던 손으로 어린 여동생을 꼭 붙잡고 언덕을 기어오르던 어느 소년의 얼굴이 생각나서.
 98|
 99|그리고 아버지의 장례식장에서 엎드려 울던 어머니의 등을 토닥이던 어린 하연이가 떠올라서.
100|
101|‘빌어먹을.’
102|
103|나는 흘러나오려는 한숨을 삼키기 위해 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
104|
105|무림과 현대는 무엇 하나 닮은 것 없는. 전혀 다른 세상이다.
106|
107|그러나 딱 하나, 사람은 변함없이 같았다.
108|
109|처음에는 이 모든 것이 게임이라 생각했던 내가 무림을 또 하나의 현실로 받아들이기 시작한 것도 그 때문이었다.
110|
111|그들도 결국 사람이었다. 분노하고, 기뻐하고, 슬퍼하는.
112|
113|죽어 마땅할 악인(惡人)도 있었고, 투명하리만치 맑은 눈을 한 선인(善人)들도 있었다.
114|
115|전자의 경우에는 한 치의 망설임도 없이 목숨을 끊었으나, 후자라면 내 목숨을 걸고 도운 적도 있었다.
116|
117|그리고 나는 지금, 이 어린 왕에게 안쓰러움을 느끼고 있다.
118|
119|파르르 떨리는 숨소리에서 조필의 습격으로 모든 것을 잃고 도망친 어린 남매를 떠올렸고, 옷소매를 꽉 붙잡은 자그마한 손을 보며 내 동생 하연이를 생각했다.
120|
121|‘냉정하게 생각해야 하는데. 반드시 그래야 하는 문제인데…….’
122|
123|아무리 생각해도 자신이 없다.
124|
125|역모냐, 순응이냐는 양자택일(兩者擇一)의 상황이 온다면 내가 이 아이를 두고 떠날 수 있을지.
126|
127|오랜 시간이 흐른 뒤에 아무렇지도 않게 그 기억을 회상할 수 있을지.
128|
129|‘거참, 여러모로 힘들게 하네.’
130|
131|나는 씁쓸하게 웃으며 가슴팍에도 닿지 않은 상산왕을 가만히 내려다보았다.
132|
133|그리고 반쯤은 충동적으로 손을 들어 머리를 툭툭 쓰다듬어 주었다.
134|
135|“……!”
136|
137|크게 뜨인 두 눈. 살짝 벌어진 입술 사이로는 지금 당장이라도 무엄하다는 일갈이라도 튀어나올 것 같았지만, 놀란 얼굴로 나를 올려다보던 상산왕은 입만 오물거릴 뿐 아무 말도 하지 않았다.
138|
139|아니, 오히려 안심하듯 내 옷소매를 힘껏 움켜쥐고 있던 손을 느슨하게 풀었다.
140|
141|지금껏 감히 그 누가 이 아이의 머리를 쓰다듬을 수 있었을까.
142|
143|저 나이 또래라면 누구나 당연하게 겪어 보았을 이 단순한 것조차도, 상산왕 주표에게는 아니었을 것이다.
144|
145|‘지금으로서는 겨우 이 정도가 내가 해 줄 수 있는 최선일 따름이고.’
146|
147|내가 내심 중얼거린 그때. 거침없이 나아가던 쌍둥이의 발걸음이 커다란 문 앞에서 멈췄다.
148|
149|철컥. 구구구궁.
150|
151|육중한 소리와 함께, 마치 살아 있는 것처럼 생생하게 용이 음각(陰刻)된 철문이 열린다. 궁 안으로 들어온 직후부터 한마디도 하지 않았던 쌍둥이가 침묵을 깨트린 것도 그때였다.
152|
153|“안으로 드십시오.”
154|
155|“안으로 드십시오.”
156|
157|어차피 더 이상 선택의 여지도 없는 상황이다.
158|
159|초절정 고수와 떨어진다는 것만으로도 듣던 중 반가운 소리.
160|
161|고개를 끄덕인 나는 상산왕을 호위하듯 앞서 철문 안으로 걸음을 내디뎠다.
162|
163|드르륵. 쿵.
164|
165|이내 다시 한번 들려오는 육중한 소음과 함께 등 뒤에서 문이 닫힌 그때. 천장에서 흐릿하게 빛나는 수많은 야명주(夜明珠)의 불빛 아래에서 한 사람이 걸음을 내디뎠다.
166|
167|저벅.
168|
169|가벼운 발걸음만큼이나 비쩍 마른 체구.
170|
171|나이는 어림잡아 오십쯤 되었을까. 소매가 바닥이 끌릴 만큼 긴 장삼을 걸친 중년인의 모습을 발견한 상산왕이 먼저 입을 열었다.
172|
173|“게 누구냐.”
174|
175|게 누구냐. 게 누구냐. 게 누구냐…….
176|
177|인적은커녕 개미 새끼 한 마리 찾아볼 수 없는 텅 빈 복도에 긴장한 목소리가 겹겹이 울려 퍼진다.
178|
179|굳은 얼굴을 한 상산왕과 비스듬히 그 앞을 가로막은 나를 물끄러미 바라보던 중년인이 입을 연 것은 메아리가 사라진 그때였다.
180|
181|“장성하신 상산왕 전하를 이리 가까이서 뵙고 보니, 지난 세월이 참으로 감개무량합니다.”
182|
183|머뭇거리던 상산왕이 물었다.
184|
185|“과인을…… 아는가?”
186|
187|“물론입니다. 전하께서는 저를 기억하지 못하시겠지만.”
188|
189|주름진 입가에 흐릿한 미소가 걸린다. 상산왕에게서 시선을 뗀 중년인이 나를 향해 고개를 돌렸다.
190|
191|“그대는 초면이군.”
192|
193|나는 대답 대신 잠시 침묵하는 것을 택했다. 중년인을 보자마자 쌍욕이 튀어나오려는 것을 간신히 참고 있었기 때문이었다.
194|
195|이유? 간단하다.
196|
197|눈앞의 중년인은, 아니 중년인‘도’ 초절정 고수였다.
198|
199|‘아니 시팔…… 진짜 더러워서 못 해 먹겠네.’
200|
201|황궁에 도착한 지 이제 겨우 이틀째다.
202|
203|그것도 말이 좋아서 이틀이지, 실제로 머무른 시간만 따지면 하루인 열두 시진도 채 지나지 않았다.
204|
205|그런데 지금까지 대면한 초절정 고수만 무려 다섯 명째.
206|
207|‘제대로 좆 됐다.’
208|
209|앞으로 옷 대신 콘돔을 입고 다녀야 하나 심각하게 고민하고 있던 그때, 중년인이 재차 입을 열었다.
210|
211|“굳이 말해 주지 않아도, 이미 그대가 누구인지는 알고 있다네. 태원진가의 진태경.”
212|
213|젠장. 이렇게 된 이상 어쩔 수 없다.
214|
215|나는 한숨을 푹 내쉬며 대답했다.
216|
217|“이 동네는 뭐 어딜 가나 다 알아보네.”
218|
219|“황실의 눈과 귀는 어디에나 존재하고, 그대는 꽤나 눈에 띄는 편이니까.”
220|
221|“잘생겨서?”
222|
223|“아니, 한눈에 보아도 무뢰배 같기 때문이지.”
224|
225|말하는 본새 보소.
226|
227|“그럼 당신은 이 황실에서 어떤 위치지? 눈? 아니면 귀?”
228|
229|“흠. 그대의 눈에 나는 무엇에 더 가까운 것 같나?”
230|
231|“청소 담당.”
232|
233|“뭐?”
234|
235|“일단 지금도 옷소매가 질질 끌리는 게, 바닥 하나는 기똥차게 닦을 것 같은데.”
236|
237|잠시 멍하니 나를 바라보던 중년인이 이내 소리 내어 웃었다.
238|
239|“하하. 듣던 대로군.”
240|
241|“듣긴 뭘 들어. 벌써 소문이라도 퍼졌나?”
242|
243|“말했잖나. 어디에나 눈과 귀가 있다고. 이미 알 만한 이들은 다 알지. 감히 황궁에 발을 디딘 어느 간 큰 강호인에게 사람 웃기는 재주가 있다는 것쯤은.”
244|
245|“그건 좀 희한하네. 나는 보통 사람을 웃기기보다는 속을 긁는 편이라.”
246|
247|“전해 들은 여러 말에서 상당히 순화했다는 표현을 깜빡했군.”
248|
249|“…….”
250|
251|“물론 말해 주는 사람마다 평가가 뒤죽박죽이라 개인적으로 궁금하기도 했지. 자, 우선 이리로.”
252|
253|대답할 틈도 없이 휙 돌아선 중년인은 자연스럽게 앞장서서 걷기 시작했다. 뒤도 돌아보지 않은 채.
254|
255|“어딜 가는 거지?”
256|
257|“재미있는 질문이군. 자네가 왜 이곳에 왔는지 잊었나?”
258|

*Unless you’re one of the Ten Kings—or maybe a master on par with the Three Saints—you’ll almost certainly be buried here.*

[P27]
People say the martial world is a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords.

[P28]
But they’re wrong.

[P29]
This was the real mountain of sabers and forest of swords. A place where the Emperor alone decided who lived and who died.

[P30]
*How many masters does he have under his command?*

[P31]
Even the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families had two Supreme Peak masters at most. Usually, they had only one. And here the Emperor had two of them working as gatekeepers.

[P32]
I felt as though I were walking along a blade’s edge.

[P33]
A bead of cold sweat slid down the back of my neck. Then I noticed a small hand tugging at my sleeve.

[P34]
Squeeze.

[P35]
The hand gripped hard enough to crumple the fabric. Only then did I notice the young prince’s ragged breathing.

[P36]
*He’s trembling.*

[P37]
Before he was a member of the imperial family or a prince, he was a child.

[P38]
He’d been one when I first met him, and he still was now.

[P39]
He’d said he left the imperial palace when he was too young to remember. Of course he wouldn’t remember the Son of Heaven, either.

[P40]
*And now his only family, his one and only older brother, is threatening his life.*

[P41]
A thought occurred to me.

[P42]
Maybe the cheerful side Prince Shangshan had shown on the way to the Imperial Capital was his way of hiding his fear and disappointment.

[P43]
When Hong Jin warned him that the Son of Heaven was a threat, he’d shaken his head and said that couldn’t be true. Maybe that was the only response a child could manage when faced with something too painful to believe.

[P44]
*He shouldn’t even have to know about any of this…but he’s had to grow up far too soon.*

[P45]
My feelings grew complicated.

[P46]
I thought of a boy from that winter in Shanxi Province, when icy winds swept through the mountains. He’d lost his parents and climbed a hill, his little fern-like hand gripping his younger sister’s tight.

[P47]
And I remembered young Hayeon patting our mother’s back as she lay facedown, sobbing at our father’s funeral.

[P48]
*Damn it.*

[P49]
I bit my lip hard to hold back a sigh.

[P50]
Murim and the modern world had nothing in common. They were completely different worlds.

[P51]
But there was one thing that never changed.

[P52]
People.

[P53]
That was why I, who’d once thought all of this was a game, had started accepting Murim as another reality.

[P54]
They were people, after all. They got angry, felt joy, and grieved.

[P55]
There were evil people who deserved to die, and good people with eyes as clear as glass.

[P56]
I’d killed the former without a moment’s hesitation. For the latter, I’d even risked my life.

[P57]
And now I felt sorry for this young prince.

[P58]
His trembling breaths reminded me of the young siblings who’d lost everything and fled after Jopil’s attack. His small hand clutching my sleeve made me think of my own little sister, Hayeon.

[P59]
*I need to think about this coldly. I have to, especially with a choice like this…*

[P60]
But no matter how much I thought about it, I wasn’t sure I could.

[P61]
If I had to choose between treason and submission, could I really leave this child behind?

[P62]
Could I look back on it years later as if it meant nothing?

[P63]
*Man, he really knows how to make things difficult.*

[P64]
I smiled bitterly and looked down at Prince Shangshan, who didn’t even reach my chest.

[P65]
Then, almost on impulse, I raised a hand and gave his head a couple of gentle pats.

[P66]
“……!”

[P67]
His eyes flew wide, and his lips parted as if he were about to shout that I’d overstepped my bounds. But Prince Shangshan only stared up at me in surprise, his mouth working soundlessly.

[P68]
Instead, his grip on my sleeve loosened, as though he felt relieved.

[P69]
Who had ever dared to pat this child on the head?

[P70]
Even something as simple as that—something other children his age took for granted—was probably unfamiliar to Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.

[P71]
*And right now, this little bit is the best I can do for him.*

[P72]
Just then, the twins, who had been striding forward without hesitation, stopped before a massive door.

[P73]
Click. Rumble.

[P74]
An iron door swung open with a heavy rumble. A dragon was carved into its surface so vividly it almost seemed alive. The twins, who hadn’t said a word since we entered the palace, broke their silence.

[P75]
“Please enter.”

[P76]
“Please enter.”

[P77]
It wasn’t as though we had any choice left. Still, hearing that we’d be separated from those Supreme Peak masters was welcome news.

[P78]
I nodded, then stepped through the iron door ahead of Prince Shangshan, shielding him as I went.

[P79]
Rrrr. Thud.

[P80]
The heavy door shut behind us. Beneath the faint light of countless night-shining pearls set into the ceiling, a man stepped forward.

[P81]
Step.

[P82]
His build was as slight as his footsteps were light.

[P83]
He looked about fifty and wore a long robe with sleeves that dragged along the floor. Prince Shangshan spoke first when he saw him.

[P84]
“Who goes there?”

[P85]
Who goes there? Who goes there? Who goes there…

[P86]
His tense voice echoed again and again through the empty corridor. Not another person in sight—not even an ant.

[P87]
The middle-aged man gazed at Prince Shangshan’s stiff face, then at me standing slightly in front of him. Only when the echoes faded did he speak.

[P88]
“To see His Highness Prince Shangshan so grown, and from this close, moves me deeply after all these years.”

[P89]
After a moment’s hesitation, Prince Shangshan asked, “Do you…know me?”

[P90]
“Of course. Though Your Highness does not remember me.”

[P91]
A faint smile touched his wrinkled lips. He turned his gaze from Prince Shangshan to me.

[P92]
“You and I have never met.”

[P93]
I said nothing. The moment I saw him, I’d had to fight to keep a string of curses from spilling out.

[P94]
Why? Simple.

[P95]
The middle-aged man in front of me—no, this middle-aged man *too*—was a Supreme Peak master.

[P96]
*Oh, for fuck’s sake… I can’t do this anymore.*

[P97]
This was only my second day at the imperial palace.

[P98]
And even that was being generous. I hadn’t actually been here for twelve shichen, a full day.

[P99]
Yet this was already the fifth Supreme Peak master I’d come face-to-face with.

[P100]
*I’m so screwed.*

[P101]
I was seriously wondering if I should start wearing a condom instead of clothes when the man spoke again.

[P102]
“You needn’t tell me who you are. I already know. Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P103]
Damn it. There was no way around it now.

[P104]
I let out a deep sigh and answered.

[P105]
“Does everyone around here recognize me wherever I go?”

[P106]
“The imperial family’s eyes and ears are everywhere. And you do stand out.”

[P107]
“Because I’m handsome?”

[P108]
“No. Because you look like a thug at first glance.”

[P109]
Listen to this guy.

[P110]
“Then what are you around here? The eyes? Or the ears?”

[P111]
“Hmm. Which do you think I’m closer to?”

[P112]
“The cleaning crew.”

[P113]
“What?”

[P114]
“Your sleeves are dragging along the floor. I bet you could give it a hell of a polish.”

[P115]
The middle-aged man stared at me blankly for a moment, then laughed aloud.

[P116]
“Ha ha. Just as I’d heard.”

[P117]
“Heard what? Are the rumors already spreading?”

[P118]
“I told you—there are eyes and ears everywhere. Everyone who needs to know already does. They’ve heard that some audacious martial artist dared to set foot in the imperial palace and has a knack for making people laugh.”

[P119]
“That’s strange. I usually get under people’s skin more than I make them laugh.”

[P120]
“I forgot to mention that ‘making people laugh’ was a considerably toned-down version of what I’d heard.”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
“Of course, the accounts were all over the place, so I was curious myself. Now, this way.”

[P123]
Before I could answer, he turned and took the lead as if it were only natural, without so much as a glance back.

[P124]
“Where are we going?”

[P125]
“Interesting question. Have you forgotten why you came here?”

[P126]
I’d had my suspicions, and I’d been right.

[P127]
Apparently, this old guy was the third transfer point on our way to the Emperor—and the final guide who would take us to our destination.

[P128]
*Obviously, he isn’t a cleaner.*

[P129]
Who the hell was he? His clothes offered no clue.

[P130]
East Depot? Or Embroidered Uniform Guard?

[P131]
His gaunt frame made him look more like a eunuch, but his voice was weighty enough to put an Embroidered Uniform Guard to shame.

[P132]
And he moved around as naturally as if this were his own home.

[P133]
*Even the twins didn’t come this far. So he must be one of the Emperor’s closest, most trusted people…*

[P134]
According to Ma Sanbao last night, the young Emperor was hot-tempered and suspicious. Only a handful of high-ranking officials and trusted servants who’d proven their loyalty were allowed into his residence, Qianqing Palace.

[P135]
And that wasn’t all.

[P136]
There were the guards, of course, along with the eunuchs and palace attendants who stayed inside to see to his every need.

[P137]
This place existed for the Emperor, by the Emperor, and in service of the Emperor.

[P138]
Could just anyone come and go in Qianqing Palace—let alone somewhere this deep inside?

[P139]
I couldn’t be sure, but he’d probably have to hold a position close to Baek Yeon’s as Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

[P140]
*Could this be the Director, the head of the East Depot? No. I heard he was much older, and he’s been bedridden with illness for years.*

[P141]
I racked my brain, but no one came to mind.

[P142]
Ma Sanbao had mentioned far too many people, and this man didn’t match the distinctive features of any of the few he’d described.

[P143]
*If only I could use my Qi Sense Skill right now…*

[P144]
But there was nothing I could do about that. If I wanted answers, I’d have to get them myself.

[P145]
I followed the man as he strolled along at an unhurried pace and tossed out a question.

[P146]
“When do I get to meet His Majesty?”

[P147]
“Soon.”

[P148]
“At this rate, we’ll get there tomorrow.”

[P149]
The man gave a short laugh without looking back.

[P150]
“You’re as impatient as you look. Wait a little. His Majesty is enjoying a diversion he hasn’t had in some time.”

[P151]
“A diversion? After summoning us?”

[P152]
“And what, do you intend to complain?”

[P153]
“……!”

[P154]
“Everyone has their place. To ascend the throne is to be able to look down upon them all. A simple enough truth of the world, isn’t it?”

[P155]
My expression hardened.

[P156]
Not because I objected to the Emperor’s behavior, or because the man’s answer had struck a nerve.

[P157]
It was the casual look on his face, his tone, the effortless authority in every small movement. And on top of that, his appearance didn’t match any of the Emperor’s confidants Ma Sanbao had mentioned.

[P158]
*No way.*

[P159]
The thought sent a groan through me.

[P160]
Step.

[P161]
The man came to an abrupt stop. Without a moment’s hesitation, he threw open the door before him, decorated with gold, silver, and jewels.

[P162]
“Your Majesty. In accordance with your solemn imperial command, I have brought the two people you requested.”

[P163]
But there was no answer.

[P164]
In fact, I couldn’t sense anyone else at all.

[P165]
Only one person stood inside the enormous bedchamber.

[P166]
The middle-aged man.

[P167]
He turned slowly toward us and smiled, showing his white teeth.

[P168]
“It was a brief diversion, but I enjoyed it.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“……!”

[P171]
A bolt of lightning shot down my spine.

Even the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families had two Supreme Peak masters at most. Usually, they had only one. And here the Emperor had two of them working as gatekeepers.

[P32]
I felt as though I were walking along a blade’s edge.

[P33]
A bead of cold sweat slid down the back of my neck. Then I noticed a small hand tugging at my sleeve.

[P34]
Squeeze.

[P35]
The hand gripped hard enough to crumple the fabric. Only then did I notice the young prince’s ragged breathing.

[P36]
*He’s trembling.*

[P37]
Before he was a member of the imperial family or a prince, he was a child.

[P38]
He’d been one when I first met him, and he still was now.

[P39]
He’d said he left the imperial palace when he was too young to remember. Of course he wouldn’t remember the Son of Heaven, either.

[P40]
*And now his only family, his one and only older brother, is threatening his life.*

[P41]
A thought occurred to me.

[P42]
Maybe the cheerful side Prince Shangshan had shown on the way to the Imperial Capital was his way of hiding his fear and disappointment.

[P43]
When Hong Jin warned him that the Son of Heaven was a threat, he’d shaken his head and said that couldn’t be true. Maybe that was the only response a child could manage when faced with something too painful to believe.

[P44]
*He shouldn’t even have to know about any of this…but he’s had to grow up far too soon.*

[P45]
My feelings grew complicated.

[P46]
I thought of a boy from that winter in Shanxi Province, when icy winds swept through the mountains. He’d lost his parents and climbed a hill, his little fern-like hand gripping his younger sister’s tight.

[P47]
And I remembered young Hayeon patting our mother’s back as she lay facedown, sobbing at our father’s funeral.

[P48]
*Damn it.*

[P49]
I bit my lip hard to hold back a sigh.

[P50]
Murim and the modern world had nothing in common. They were completely different worlds.

[P51]
But there was one thing that never changed.

[P52]
People.

[P53]
That was why I, who’d once thought all of this was a game, had started accepting Murim as another reality.

[P54]
They were people, after all. They got angry, felt joy, and grieved.

[P55]
There were evil people who deserved to die, and good people with eyes as clear as glass.

[P56]
I’d killed the former without a moment’s hesitation. For the latter, I’d even risked my life.

[P57]
And now I felt sorry for this young prince.

[P58]
His trembling breaths reminded me of the young siblings who’d lost everything and fled after Jopil’s attack. His small hand clutching my sleeve made me think of my own little sister, Hayeon.

[P59]
*I need to think about this coldly. I have to, especially with a choice like this…*

[P60]
But no matter how much I thought about it, I wasn’t sure I could.

[P61]
If I had to choose between treason and submission, could I really leave this child behind?

[P62]
Could I look back on it years later as if it meant nothing?

[P63]
*Man, he really knows how to make things difficult.*

[P64]
I smiled bitterly and looked down at Prince Shangshan, who didn’t even reach my chest.

[P65]
Then, almost on impulse, I raised a hand and gave his head a couple of gentle pats.

[P66]
“……!”

[P67]
His eyes flew wide, and his lips parted as if he were about to shout that I’d overstepped my bounds. But Prince Shangshan only stared up at me in surprise, his mouth working soundlessly.

[P68]
Instead, his grip on my sleeve loosened, as though he felt relieved.

[P69]
Who had ever dared to pat this child on the head?

[P70]
Even something as simple as that—something other children his age took for granted—was probably unfamiliar to Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.

[P71]
*And right now, this little bit is the best I can do for him.*

[P72]
Just then, the twins, who had been striding forward without hesitation, stopped before a massive door.

[P73]
Click. Rumble.

[P74]
An iron door swung open with a heavy rumble. A dragon was carved into its surface so vividly it almost seemed alive. The twins, who hadn’t said a word since we entered the palace, broke their silence.

[P75]
“Please enter.”

[P76]
“Please enter.”

[P77]
It wasn’t as though we had any choice left. Still, hearing that we’d be separated from those Supreme Peak masters was welcome news.

[P78]
I nodded, then stepped through the iron door ahead of Prince Shangshan, shielding him as I went.

[P79]
Rrrr. Thud.

[P80]
The heavy door shut behind us. Beneath the faint light of countless night-shining pearls set into the ceiling, a man stepped forward.

[P81]
Step.

[P82]
His build was as slight as his footsteps were light.

[P83]
He looked about fifty and wore a long robe with sleeves that dragged along the floor. Prince Shangshan spoke first when he saw him.

[P84]
“Who goes there?”

[P85]
Who goes there? Who goes there? Who goes there…

[P86]
His tense voice echoed again and again through the empty corridor. Not another person in sight—not even an ant.

[P87]
The middle-aged man gazed at Prince Shangshan’s stiff face, then at me standing slightly in front of him. Only when the echoes faded did he speak.

[P88]
“To see His Highness Prince Shangshan so grown, and from this close, moves me deeply after all these years.”

[P89]
After a moment’s hesitation, Prince Shangshan asked, “Do you…know me?”

[P90]
“Of course. Though Your Highness does not remember me.”

[P91]
A faint smile touched his wrinkled lips. He turned his gaze from Prince Shangshan to me.

[P92]
“You and I have never met.”

[P93]
I said nothing. The moment I saw him, I’d had to fight to keep a string of curses from spilling out.

[P94]
Why? Simple.

[P95]
The middle-aged man in front of me—no, this middle-aged man *too*—was a Supreme Peak master.

[P96]
*Oh, for fuck’s sake… I can’t do this anymore.*

[P97]
This was only my second day at the imperial palace.

[P98]
And even that was being generous. I hadn’t actually been here for twelve shichen, a full day.

[P99]
Yet this was already the fifth Supreme Peak master I’d come face-to-face with.

[P100]
*I’m so screwed.*

[P101]
I was seriously wondering if I should start wearing a condom instead of clothes when the man spoke again.

[P102]
“You needn’t tell me who you are. I already know. Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P103]
Damn it. There was no way around it now.

[P104]
I let out a deep sigh and answered.

[P105]
“Does everyone around here recognize me wherever I go?”

[P106]
“The imperial family’s eyes and ears are everywhere. And you do stand out.”

[P107]
“Because I’m handsome?”

[P108]
“No. Because you look like a thug at first glance.”

[P109]
Listen to this guy.

[P110]
“Then what are you around here? The eyes? Or the ears?”

[P111]
“Hmm. Which do you think I’m closer to?”

[P112]
“The cleaning crew.”

[P113]
“What?”

[P114]
“Your sleeves are dragging along the floor. I bet you could give it a hell of a polish.”

[P115]
The middle-aged man stared at me blankly for a moment, then laughed aloud.

[P116]
“Ha ha. Just as I’d heard.”

[P117]
“Heard what? Are the rumors already spreading?”

[P118]
“I told you—there are eyes and ears everywhere. Everyone who needs to know already does. They’ve heard that some audacious martial artist dared to set foot in the imperial palace and has a knack for making people laugh.”

[P119]
“That’s strange. I usually get under people’s skin more than I make them laugh.”

[P120]
“I forgot to mention that ‘making people laugh’ was a considerably toned-down version of what I’d heard.”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
“Of course, the accounts were all over the place, so I was curious myself. Now, this way.”

[P123]
Before I could answer, he turned and took the lead as if it were only natural, without so much as a glance back.

[P124]
“Where are we going?”

[P125]
“Interesting question. Have you forgotten why you came here?”

[P126]
I’d had my suspicions, and I’d been right.

[P127]
Apparently, this old guy was the third transfer point on our way to the Emperor—and the final guide who would take us to our destination.

[P128]
*Obviously, he isn’t a cleaner.*

[P129]
Who the hell was he? His clothes offered no clue.

[P130]
East Depot? Or Embroidered Uniform Guard?

[P131]
His gaunt frame made him look more like a eunuch, but his voice was weighty enough to put an Embroidered Uniform Guard to shame.

[P132]
And he moved around as naturally as if this were his own home.

[P133]
*Even the twins didn’t come this far. So he must be one of the Emperor’s closest, most trusted people…*

[P134]
According to Ma Sanbao last night, the young Emperor was hot-tempered and suspicious. Only a handful of high-ranking officials and trusted servants who’d proven their loyalty were allowed into his residence, Qianqing Palace.

[P135]
And that wasn’t all.

[P136]
There were the guards, of course, along with the eunuchs and palace attendants who stayed inside to see to his every need.

[P137]
This place existed for the Emperor, by the Emperor, and in service of the Emperor.

[P138]
Could just anyone come and go in Qianqing Palace—let alone somewhere this deep inside?

[P139]
I couldn’t be sure, but he’d probably have to hold a position close to Baek Yeon’s as Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

[P140]
*Could this be the Director, the head of the East Depot? No. I heard he was much older, and he’s been bedridden with illness for years.*

[P141]
I racked my brain, but no one came to mind.

[P142]
Ma Sanbao had mentioned far too many people, and this man didn’t match the distinctive features of any of the few he’d described.

[P143]
*If only I could use my Qi Sense Skill right now…*

[P144]
But there was nothing I could do about that. If I wanted answers, I’d have to get them myself.

[P145]
I followed the man as he strolled along at an unhurried pace and tossed out a question.

[P146]
“When do I get to meet His Majesty?”

[P147]
“Soon.”

[P148]
“At this rate, we’ll get there tomorrow.”

[P149]
The man gave a short laugh without looking back.

[P150]
“You’re as impatient as you look. Wait a little. His Majesty is enjoying a diversion he hasn’t had in some time.”

[P151]
“A diversion? After summoning us?”

[P152]
“And what, do you intend to complain?”

[P153]
“……!”

[P154]
“Everyone has their place. To ascend the throne is to be able to look down upon them all. A simple enough truth of the world, isn’t it?”

[P155]
My expression hardened.

[P156]
Not because I objected to the Emperor’s behavior, or because the man’s answer had struck a nerve.

[P157]
It was the casual look on his face, his tone, the effortless authority in every small movement. And on top of that, his appearance didn’t match any of the Emperor’s confidants Ma Sanbao had mentioned.

[P158]
*No way.*

[P159]
The thought sent a groan through me.

[P160]
Step.

[P161]
The man came to an abrupt stop. Without a moment’s hesitation, he threw open the door before him, decorated with gold, silver, and jewels.

[P162]
“Your Majesty. In accordance with your solemn imperial command, I have brought the two people you requested.”

[P163]
But there was no answer.

[P164]
In fact, I couldn’t sense anyone else at all.

[P165]
Only one person stood inside the enormous bedchamber.

[P166]
The middle-aged man.

[P167]
He turned slowly toward us and smiled, showing his white teeth.

[P168]
“It was a brief diversion, but I enjoyed it.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“……!”

[P171]
A bolt of lightning shot down my spine.

*They’ve definitely trained in a combined attack technique…but what martial art, exactly?*

[P19]
No matter how I looked at it, the situation was bad.

[P20]

[P21]
And on top of that…

[P22]
*Why the hell are there so many bats?*

[P23]
Shadows hidden even in the faint light.

[P24]
The people watching our every move from the darkness had to be guards raised by the imperial family—and assassins.

[P25]
If the worst happened, those assassins, nearly a hundred of them, would carve me up with the one-strike killing techniques they’d spent their lives honing. And the twin Supreme Peak masters would be right there with them, wielding a combined technique they looked as if they’d learned in the womb.

[P26]
*Unless you’re one of the Ten Kings—or maybe a master on par with the Three Saints—you’ll almost certainly be buried here.*

[P27]
People say the martial world is a mountain of sabers and a forest of swords.

But they’re wrong.

[P29]
This was the real mountain of sabers and forest of swords. A place where the Emperor alone decided who lived and who died.

[P30]
*How many masters does he have under his command?*

[P31]
Even the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families had two Supreme Peak masters at most. Usually, they had only one. And here the Emperor had two of them working as gatekeepers.

I felt as though I were walking along a blade’s edge.

[P34]
Squeeze.

[P36]
*He’s trembling.*

[P37]
Before he was a member of the imperial family or a prince, he was a child.

[P38]
He’d been one when I first met him, and he still was now.

[P39]
He’d said he left the imperial palace when he was too young to remember. Of course he wouldn’t remember the Son of Heaven, either.

[P40]
*And now his only family, his one and only older brother, is threatening his life.*

[P41]
A thought occurred to me.

[P42]
Maybe the cheerful side Prince Shangshan had shown on the way to the Imperial Capital was his way of hiding his fear and disappointment.

[P43]
When Hong Jin warned him that the Son of Heaven was a threat, he’d shaken his head and said that couldn’t be true. Maybe that was the only response a child could manage when faced with something too painful to believe.

[P44]
*He shouldn’t even have to know about any of this…but he’s had to grow up far too soon.*

[P45]
My feelings grew complicated.

[P46]
I thought of a boy from that winter in Shanxi Province, when icy winds swept through the mountains. He’d lost his parents and climbed a hill, his little fern-like hand gripping his younger sister’s tight.

[P47]
And I remembered young Hayeon patting our mother’s back as she lay facedown, sobbing at our father’s funeral.

[P48]
*Damn it.*

[P49]
I bit my lip hard to hold back a sigh.

[P50]
Murim and the modern world had nothing in common. They were completely different worlds.

[P51]
But there was one thing that never changed.

[P52]
People.

[P53]
That was why I, who’d once thought all of this was a game, had started accepting Murim as another reality.

[P54]
They were people, after all. They got angry, felt joy, and grieved.

[P55]
There were evil people who deserved to die, and good people with eyes as clear as glass.

[P56]
I’d killed the former without a moment’s hesitation. For the latter, I’d even risked my life.

[P57]
And now I felt sorry for this young prince.

[P58]
His trembling breaths reminded me of the young siblings who’d lost everything and fled after Jopil’s attack. His small hand clutching my sleeve made me think of my own little sister, Hayeon.

[P59]
*I need to think about this coldly. I have to, especially with a choice like this…*

[P60]
But no matter how much I thought about it, I wasn’t sure I could.

[P61]
If I had to choose between treason and submission, could I really leave this child behind?

[P62]
Could I look back on it years later as if it meant nothing?

[P63]
*Man, he really knows how to make things difficult.*

[P64]
I smiled bitterly and looked down at Prince Shangshan, who didn’t even reach my chest.

[P65]
Then, almost on impulse, I raised a hand and gave his head a couple of gentle pats.

[P66]
“……!”

[P67]
His eyes flew wide, and his lips parted as if he were about to shout that I’d overstepped my bounds. But Prince Shangshan only stared up at me in surprise, his mouth working soundlessly.

[P68]
Instead, his grip on my sleeve loosened, as though he felt relieved.

[P69]
Who had ever dared to pat this child on the head?

[P70]
Even something as simple as that—something other children his age took for granted—was probably unfamiliar to Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao.

[P71]
*And right now, this little bit is the best I can do for him.*

[P72]
Just then, the twins, who had been striding forward without hesitation, stopped before a massive door.

Click. Rumble.

[P75]
“Please enter.”

[P76]
“Please enter.”

[P77]

[P78]
I nodded, then stepped through the iron door ahead of Prince Shangshan, shielding him as I went.

[P79]
Rrrr. Thud.

[P80]
The heavy door shut behind us. Beneath the faint light of countless night-shining pearls set into the ceiling, a man stepped forward.

[P81]
Step.

[P82]
His build was as slight as his footsteps were light.

[P83]
He looked about fifty and wore a long robe with sleeves that dragged along the floor. Prince Shangshan spoke first when he saw him.

[P84]
“Who goes there?”

[P85]
Who goes there? Who goes there? Who goes there…

[P86]
His tense voice echoed again and again through the empty corridor. Not another person in sight—not even an ant.

[P87]
The middle-aged man gazed at Prince Shangshan’s stiff face, then at me standing slightly in front of him. Only when the echoes faded did he speak.

[P88]
“To see His Highness Prince Shangshan so grown, and from this close, moves me deeply after all these years.”

[P89]
After a moment’s hesitation, Prince Shangshan asked, “Do you…know me?”

[P90]
“Of course. Though Your Highness does not remember me.”

[P91]
A faint smile touched his wrinkled lips. He turned his gaze from Prince Shangshan to me.

[P92]
“You and I have never met.”

[P93]
I said nothing. The moment I saw him, I’d had to fight to keep a string of curses from spilling out.

[P94]
Why? Simple.

[P95]
The middle-aged man in front of me—no, this middle-aged man *too*—was a Supreme Peak master.

[P96]
*Oh, for fuck’s sake… I can’t do this anymore.*

[P97]
This was only my second day at the imperial palace.

[P98]
And even that was being generous. I hadn’t actually been here for twelve shichen, a full day.

[P99]
Yet this was already the fifth Supreme Peak master I’d come face-to-face with.

[P100]
*I’m so screwed.*

[P101]
I was seriously wondering if I should start wearing a condom instead of clothes when the man spoke again.

[P102]
“You needn’t tell me who you are. I already know. Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P103]
Damn it. There was no way around it now.

[P104]
I let out a deep sigh and answered.

[P105]
“Does everyone around here recognize me wherever I go?”

[P106]
“The imperial family’s eyes and ears are everywhere. And you do stand out.”

[P107]
“Because I’m handsome?”

[P108]
“No. Because you look like a thug at first glance.”

[P109]
Listen to this guy.

[P110]
“Then what are you around here? The eyes? Or the ears?”

[P111]
“Hmm. Which do you think I’m closer to?”

[P112]
“The cleaning crew.”

[P113]
“What?”

[P114]
“Your sleeves are dragging along the floor. I bet you could give it a hell of a polish.”

[P115]
The middle-aged man stared at me blankly for a moment, then laughed aloud.

[P116]
“Ha ha. Just as I’d heard.”

[P117]
“Heard what? Are the rumors already spreading?”

[P118]
“I told you—there are eyes and ears everywhere. Everyone who needs to know already does. They’ve heard that some audacious martial artist dared to set foot in the imperial palace and has a knack for making people laugh.”

[P119]
“That’s strange. I usually get under people’s skin more than I make them laugh.”

[P120]
“I forgot to mention that ‘making people laugh’ was a considerably toned-down version of what I’d heard.”

[P121]
“……”

[P122]
“Of course, the accounts were all over the place, so I was curious myself. Now, this way.”

[P123]
Before I could answer, he turned and took the lead as if it were only natural, without so much as a glance back.

[P124]
“Where are we going?”

[P125]
“Interesting question. Have you forgotten why you came here?”

[P126]
I’d had my suspicions, and I’d been right.

[P127]
Apparently, this old guy was the third transfer point on our way to the Emperor—and the final guide who would take us to our destination.

[P128]
*Obviously, he isn’t a cleaner.*

[P129]
Who the hell was he? His clothes offered no clue.

[P130]
East Depot? Or Embroidered Uniform Guard?

[P131]
His gaunt frame made him look more like a eunuch, but his voice was weighty enough to put an Embroidered Uniform Guard to shame.

[P132]
And he moved around as naturally as if this were his own home.

[P133]
*Even the twins didn’t come this far. So he must be one of the Emperor’s closest, most trusted people…*

[P134]
According to Ma Sanbao last night, the young Emperor was hot-tempered and suspicious. Only a handful of high-ranking officials and trusted servants who’d proven their loyalty were allowed into his residence, Qianqing Palace.

[P135]
And that wasn’t all.

[P136]
There were the guards, of course, along with the eunuchs and palace attendants who stayed inside to see to his every need.

[P137]
This place existed for the Emperor, by the Emperor, and in service of the Emperor.

[P138]
Could just anyone come and go in Qianqing Palace—let alone somewhere this deep inside?

[P139]
I couldn’t be sure, but he’d probably have to hold a position close to Baek Yeon’s as Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

[P140]
*Could this be the Director, the head of the East Depot? No. I heard he was much older, and he’s been bedridden with illness for years.*

[P141]
I racked my brain, but no one came to mind.

[P142]
Ma Sanbao had mentioned far too many people, and this man didn’t match the distinctive features of any of the few he’d described.

[P143]
*If only I could use my Qi Sense Skill right now…*

[P144]
But there was nothing I could do about that. If I wanted answers, I’d have to get them myself.

[P145]
I followed the man as he strolled along at an unhurried pace and tossed out a question.

[P146]
“When do I get to meet His Majesty?”

[P147]
“Soon.”

[P148]
“At this rate, we’ll get there tomorrow.”

[P149]
The man gave a short laugh without looking back.

[P150]
“You’re as impatient as you look. Wait a little. His Majesty is enjoying a diversion he hasn’t had in some time.”

[P151]
“A diversion? After summoning us?”

[P152]
“And what, do you intend to complain?”

[P153]
“……!”

[P154]
“Everyone has their place. To ascend the throne is to be able to look down upon them all. A simple enough truth of the world, isn’t it?”

[P155]
My expression hardened.

[P156]
Not because I objected to the Emperor’s behavior, or because the man’s answer had struck a nerve.

[P157]
It was the casual look on his face, his tone, the effortless authority in every small movement. And on top of that, his appearance didn’t match any of the Emperor’s confidants Ma Sanbao had mentioned.

[P158]
*No way.*

[P159]
The thought sent a groan through me.

[P160]
Step.

[P161]
The man came to an abrupt stop. Without a moment’s hesitation, he threw open the door before him, decorated with gold, silver, and jewels.

[P162]
“Your Majesty. In accordance with your solemn imperial command, I have brought the two people you requested.”

[P163]
But there was no answer.

[P164]
In fact, I couldn’t sense anyone else at all.

[P165]
Only one person stood inside the enormous bedchamber.

[P166]
The middle-aged man.

[P167]
He turned slowly toward us and smiled, showing his white teeth.

[P168]
“It was a brief diversion, but I enjoyed it.”

[P169]
“……!”

[P170]
“……!”

[P171]
A bolt of lightning shot down my spine.
